mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille Convention destinations: certified copy issued by the New Zealand Companies Office to be certified and then submitted to the Department of Internal Affairs in Auckland, Wellington or Christchurch for an Apostille. For non-member destinations: certified copy to be forwarded to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade for pre-authentication, then to the destination country consulate for Consular Legalization. Apostille and Consular Legalization are mutually exclusive alternative paths and must never be chained sequentially.

For Apostille member states: Certificate of Good Standing is extracted from the Companies Register and then apostillised by the Department of Internal Affairs. For non-member states: the certificate must be authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade and then legalised by the consular section of the relevant destination state. Only one route may be used; never combine Apostille and Consular Legalization on the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Board of Directors; notarised by a New Zealand Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The executed Board Resolution and Power of Attorney must first be notarised by a New Zealand Notary Public. For an Apostille member state, the notarised instrument is then apostillised by the Department of Internal Affairs. For a non-member destination, the notarised instrument is legalised by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade and then by the destination embassy or consulate. The two authentication paths are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: New Zealand Company and founding shareholders; certified by the Company Secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The constitution must be certified by the company secretary and, if requested, notarised. For Apostille Convention states, the document goes to the Department of Internal Affairs for an Apostille. For non-member states, the document goes through Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade certification and then Consular Legalization at the receiving state's diplomatic mission. Apostille and Consular Legalization are alternative, exclusive modes; they may not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered trading bank in New Zealand
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank reference letter must be signed under seal by a bank officer and notarised by a New Zealand notary. For an Apostille jurisdiction it then receives an Apostille from the Department of Internal Affairs. For a non-Apostille jurisdiction it must be legalised by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade and then by the receiving consulate. Apostille and Consular Legalization are mutually exclusive routes and may never be undertaken sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening shall be performed in two tiers before incorporation. Tier one: all directors, shareholders above 25 percent, ultimate beneficial owners, and any authorized signatories must be screened against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, New Zealand Financial Markets Authority AML/CFT Watchlist, domestic New Zealand Police notices, and Interpol I-24/7 notes. Tier two: all politically exposed persons, including persons holding prominent public functions in China, New Zealand, or third countries, and their close associates or family members, require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, and senior management approval. Screening shall be repeated within 24 hours of incorporation and again at every material change of control. Any positive match triggers immediate suspension of the formation process and the filing of a Suspicious Transaction Report with the New Zealand Financial Intelligence Unit under section 40 of the AML/CFT Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office - Companies Register Online Name Reservation Platform
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory doctrine requires the legal company name to be rendered in Latin script. English and Te Reo Maori names are both acceptable but must appear in the New Zealand Companies Register using the official Latin-script spelling, including macrons where Maori words are used. The four-tier naming convention is: (1) exact legal name in Latin script; (2) phonetic transliteration compliant with New Zealand gazette practice where the name is used in foreign-language commercial contexts; (3) prohibited and sensitive token screening; and (4) trade mark and domain name conflict clearance limited to the Latin-script variant. Any name containing non-Latin script must be transliterated into English for registration; the non-Latin script may be preserved in an ancillary trademark filing but does not form part of the legal company name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon receiving a formal name rejection, the applicant shall request written reasons from the New Zealand Companies Office within 15 working days of the decision. The applicant should then submit a formal appeal to the Registrar of Companies under the Companies Act 1993, accompanied by the automated refusal reference, a statutory declaration setting out compliance with the four-tier naming protocol, and proof that the proposed name does not infringe any registered trade mark or suggest Crown, statutory, or regulatory sponsorship. The Registrar shall be asked to reconsider whether the name is intentionally misleading or materially indistinguishable from an existing registered name. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may apply to the High Court for judicial review under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016 within 28 days of notification of the final decision. As a parallel remedy, the applicant may immediately reserve a new name and proceed with incorporation under the alternative name while the appeal is pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not categorically rejected by Inland Revenue for GST registration purposes, but it is unacceptable as a registered office under section 336 of the Companies Act 1993 because the registered office must be a physical street address in New Zealand accessible to the public during ordinary business hours. Banks, including those supporting Stripe and PayPal settlement rails, generally require a New Zealand physical presence, a street address for director and shareholder correspondence, and evidence of operational substance such as a lease, service agreement, or local agent arrangement. A virtual office may be tolerated as an ancillary service address for correspondence where the company maintains a physical registered office location and meets the New Zealand commercial substance expectations of the Financial Markets Authority and the major clearing banks. For an esports tournament platform operating without a statutory license, an unattended virtual mailbox will be treated as a high-risk indicator by onboarding banks and may result in account refusal or enhanced due diligence conditions.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: low to moderate, estimated at 10 percent per tax year for an unannounced on-site inspection by Inland Revenue or the Companies Office where the company has no brick-and-mortar premises. The risk increases materially if the virtual address is shared by more than five entities, if the company shows high turnover with foreign directors, or if there are repeated manual GST filing anomalies. Inspection checklist: (1) verify registered office is a physical street address not a PO box; (2) check for signage and physical records at the registered office; (3) confirm compliance with section 336 access obligations; (4) inspect for local staff, duty directors, or a resident agent; (5) verify that bank statements, board minutes, and statutory registers are kept at a New Zealand address; (6) assess actual esports platform operations including server locations, payment flow documentation, and tournament service agreements. Maintaining an active physical office, modern records, and local corporate secretarial support reduces the annual inspection probability to below 10 percent.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (Public Act 1993 No 105), as amended, principally Parts 2, 3, 4, 8 and 12 dealing with incorporation, share capital, registered office, directors and financial reporting, together with the Financial Reporting Act 2013 for reporting and audit obligations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), Wellington, New Zealand.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Company (online Incorporation Application through the New Zealand Companies Office RealMe authenticated service).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. No minimum paid-up capital is required under the Companies Act 1993 and no blocked escrow account or statutory capital deposit exists. At least one share must be issued; the board must approve consideration and record allotment in the share register. At least one director must live in New Zealand, and any foreign-resident director must be appointed only alongside a New Zealand-resident director unless an applicable exception is satisfied.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (THE "COMPANY"), BEING DULY CONVENED AND HELD IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE COMPANIES ACT 1993 AND THE CONSTITUTION OF THE COMPANY. 1. REGISTERED OFFICE AND ADDRESS FOR SERVICE: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company in New Zealand be adopted as [●], New Zealand, and that such address be filed with the Registrar of Companies as the Company's registered office and address for service, subject to the right of the board to change the registered office and address for service by resolution and proper notification to the Registrar. 2. SUBSCRIPTION AND ALLOTMENT OF SHARES: RESOLVED that the initial ordinary shares of the Company be subscribed for and allotted as follows: [name of subscriber] shall subscribe for [●] ordinary shares at an issue price of NZD [●] per share, and that the consideration for the shares, being NZD [●] in cash or the transfer of assets as may be approved, be accepted by the Company. RESOLVED further that the allotments be recorded in the register of shareholders and that share certificates be issued in the approved form of the Company. 3. BANKING ARRANGEMENTS: RESOLVED that [name and branch of bank] be appointed as the Company's principal bank, that the officers of the Company be authorized to open current, savings, and foreign currency accounts, and that the bank mandate require [two] of the following authorized signatories, namely the Managing Director, Chief Financial Officer, and Company Secretary, to sign separately or jointly as specified in the account mandate. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY AND CORPORATE OFFICERS: RESOLVED that [name] be appointed as Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Company, that [name] be appointed as Chief Financial Officer, and that [name] be appointed as Company Secretary, each with authority to act in the ordinary course of the Company's business, to engage contractors, to sign contracts, and to cause the statutory registers and filings of the Company to be maintained. 5. AUDIT AND COMPLIANCE: RESOLVED that the board assess whether the Company is required to appoint an auditor under the Financial Reporting Act 2013 and, if required, that [name] be appointed as auditor. RESOLVED further that the directors and officers are hereby directed to take all steps necessary to ensure compliance with the Companies Act 1993, the Financial Reporting Act 2013, the Income Tax Act 2007, the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, and applicable anti-money laundering legislation. 6. AUTHORIZATION OF FILINGS: RESOLVED that any director or the Company Secretary be and is hereby authorized to complete, sign and deliver all applications, consents, statutory declarations and notices, and to certify a copy of these resolutions to banks, regulators, and other third parties as required. DATED this [●] day of [●] 20[●]. /s/ CHAIRPERSON.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve company name and obtain preliminary availability clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office Name Reservation Portal (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit up to three proposed names through the New Zealand Companies Office online name reservation service after conducting a real-time search of the Companies Register. The proposed name must not be identical or nearly identical to an existing name, must not be offensive, and must not imply a regulated activity unless the necessary permission is obtained. If the desired name contains a restricted word such as bank, trust, or university, upload the appropriate consent from the relevant regulator. For overseas applicants, upload a notarized copy of the passport or government-issued photographic identity document. The name reservation is valid for 20 working days, and the reservation may be renewed before expiry if incorporation is not completed within that period.
required_dossiers: Proposed company names (up to three)
Applicant identity verification through RealMe or notarized photographic identification
Written consent or regulator approval for any restricted word
Name availability search report or screen capture from the Companies Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, revise the proposed name list and resubmit online. If an existing rights holder objects, obtain written consent and upload that consent to the Companies Office. If the reservation expires, renew it online at no additional cost or reserve a new name and link it to the pending incorporation application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the company incorporation application and obtain the certificate of incorporation and NZBN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office / Registrar of Companies (MBIE), online Incorporate Company service via RealMe login
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online incorporation application and enter the reserved company name, the registered office physical address in New Zealand, the address for service, the full legal names and residential addresses of all directors and shareholders, the share allocation, and any adopted constitution. At least one director must confirm a New Zealand residential address. Upload signed consents to act as director for each director, verified identity documents, and any notarized or apostilled foreign documents. Verify that the registered office is not a post office box and that the address for service is valid in New Zealand. Submit the application and pay the prescribed filing fee in New Zealand dollars. Upon successful registration, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation and automatically assigns a New Zealand Business Number (NZBN).
required_dossiers: Reserved company name approval
Constitution (optional; if omitted, the Companies Act 1993 default rules apply)
Signed consent to act as director for each proposed director
Full legal name, residential address, date of birth, and identity verification for each director
Full legal name, residential address, and share allocation for each shareholder
Physical registered office address and address for service within New Zealand
Payment of the incorporation filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar queries the application, submit the required correction through the Companies Office online portal within five working days. If the application is suspended, the applicant should provide the missing consent, identity document, or statutory declaration and request accelerated re-processing. If the application is rejected, amend the defective data, reserve a new name if necessary, and resubmit the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with Inland Revenue for income tax, GST, PAYE, and other business tax obligations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD), New Zealand, through the myIR secure online portal and IRD business registration desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, enrol the company for online services in myIR using the IRD number notified by Inland Revenue on the company's registration. Register for goods and services tax (GST) if the company's annual turnover is expected to exceed NZD 60,000 or if voluntary registration is desired. If the company will employ staff, register as an employer for PAYE and KiwiSaver purposes. If employer-provided benefits are anticipated, register for fringe benefit tax (FBT). The company should notify IRD of its New Zealand addresses, actual business activity, and estimated financial year end. For non-resident-owned companies, the board should assess non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) and approved issuer levy (AIL) obligations on shareholder loans, dividends, or interest payments.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Company IRD number as notified by Inland Revenue
Full names, tax residency status, and IRD numbers of directors and significant shareholders
Company business activity description and estimated annual turnover
Payroll plans, including number of employees and expected remuneration
Bank account details for IRD refund and payment purposes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD number is not received automatically after incorporation, contact the IRD business line or submit an IRD number application through myIR with the Certificate of Incorporation attached. If IRD records contain incorrect company details, first correct the Companies Office register, which will update Inland Revenue, and then submit any remaining correction to myIR. If a GST or payroll registration application is suspended, supply the missing company and director information within 10 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Hold the first board meeting, adopt corporate governance minutes, issue share certificates, and open the corporate bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the company under the Companies Act 1993 and the company constitution; principal bank authorized by the board under New Zealand anti-money laundering requirements
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a valid first board meeting in person or by unanimous written resolution. The board must adopt the first board resolutions covering the registered office, allotment and issue of shares, banking authorization, and appointment of officers. Issue share certificates to the subscribers and enter the allotments in the company's share register within 10 working days after allotment. Prepare and retain signed minutes and board consents. Use the board minutes, Certificate of Incorporation, constitution, and director identification to open a corporate bank account. For directors and ultimate beneficial owners who are not New Zealand residents, provide notarized passports, proof of address, and a reference from an existing banker if requested. The bank must complete customer due diligence in accordance with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009 before the account is activated.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN
Constitution and first board resolutions
Register of directors and register of shareholders
Share certificates for all issued shares
Board meeting minutes signed by the chairperson
Identity documents, residential address proof, and notarized passports for foreign directors
Beneficial ownership declaration and bank know-your-customer forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires further customer due diligence evidence, supply a certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation, a current company extract from the Companies Register, and an updated beneficial ownership statement. If a board resolution is challenged by the bank or a regulator, ratify the resolution at a subsequent board meeting and provide a signed written resolution confirming the validation of all prior actions.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - pure digital software publishing and esports community platform activity under ISIC 5820 involves no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing operation requiring an industrial license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating permit, manufacturing license, or premises operating license is required for the registered digital business activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - no environmental impact assessment trigger under the Resource Management Act 1991 for office-based software publishing; the Environmental Protection Authority of New Zealand would have jurisdiction only for nationally significant activities, none of which are triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no industrial wastewater, point-source volatile organic compound emissions, hazardous waste stream, or trade waste discharge will be generated by the esports community platform activities; only ordinary domestic-grade office waste and standard cloud hosting electricity consumption are expected.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable - no Civil Defence fire permit, dangerous goods storage approval, or restricted occupancy license is required for pure digital or consulting operations. The company must remain compliant with the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 for any employees, and if occupying a commercial office, the landlord must maintain a current building warrant of fitness covering fire safety, means of escape, and structural clearance for the leased premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD; Te Tari Taake) is the sole national tax authority for income tax and GST administration. The official electronic portal is myIR at www.ird.govt.nz, supplemented by accredited third-party software filing gateways.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident company must first determine whether it has sufficient New Zealand nexus (carrying on a taxable activity through a fixed establishment, deriving New Zealand-source service income, or supplying remote/digital services to New Zealand consumers). If nexus exists, the company must obtain an IRD number, which is the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN). For a foreign non-resident entity, the procedure is: (1) complete Inland Revenue form IR596, the prescribed application for an IRD number for a non-resident company, accompanied by certified copies of the certificate of incorporation, constitutional documents, director and shareholder details, and the entity's resolution appointing a New Zealand tax agent or representative; (2) lodge the application directly with the IRD or electronically through a New Zealand tax agent via myIR; (3) receive the IRD number, which is the same numeric identifier later used for GST registration; (4) separately complete GST registration on form IR356 or through myIR if the company makes or intends to make taxable supplies in New Zealand and exceeds the NZD 60,000 annual registration threshold, or if it elects voluntary GST registration under the remote services regime; (5) maintain an active myIR account for all assessment, return filing, and communication obligations. For digital businesses selling esports community platform services to New Zealand residential consumers, the simplified non-resident GST registration path applies through myIR, allowing the IRD number and GST number to be issued without a physical New Zealand establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available. A close-held company satisfying the statutory criteria may elect to become a Look-Through Company (LTC) under the Income Tax Act 2007, which shifts certain taxable income and deductions through to shareholders. New Zealand also imposes mandatory hybrid and branch mismatch rules under the Taxation (Neutralising Base Erosion and Profit Shifting) Act 2018, which are not elective and operate as anti-avoidance provisions. No United States-style check-the-box election exists in New Zealand domestic tax law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) as enacted under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 in any 12-month period for supplies made in New Zealand and for remote/digital services supplied by non-resident suppliers to New Zealand resident consumers, calculated on the total value of taxable supplies to New Zealand; voluntary registration is also available in prescribed circumstances.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not impose a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance system, statutory e-invoicing API, or anti-fraud digital stamping mechanism. Taxpayers may issue GST invoices in a commercially agreed electronic or paper format provided the invoice includes the legally required details (supplier and recipient names, GST-inclusive pricing, GST component, date, and supply description). The voluntary e-invoicing framework operates on the Peppol network as an optional interoperability standard. GST returns are lodged through myIR or accredited software on frequency bands (monthly, two-monthly, or six-monthly) determined by the taxpayer's taxable turnover. The IRD enforces compliance through traditional records inspection, data matching, and cross-border information exchange, rather than upfront invoice pre-clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods may be zero-rated under section 11 of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985 where the supplier causes the goods to be physically exported from New Zealand and retains credible documentary evidence of the exportation. Services may be zero-rated under section 11A where the services are supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside New Zealand at the time of supply, and the services are not supplied in connection with New Zealand land or New Zealand goods. For the esports community platform business model, tournament entry fees, matchmaking subscriptions, virtual item purchases, and broadcast or community services supplied to non-resident users located outside New Zealand may be zero-rated where the supplier obtains and preserves conclusive evidence of each recipient's offshore location, such as payment gateway billing address, IP address, ISP location data, mobile country codes, and any contract or user database showing a non-New Zealand residential address. Supplies of remote digital services to New Zealand consumers are instead standard-rated at 15%. The zero-rating claim must be substantiated at the time of supply and retained for audit.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Inland Revenue Department may audit any zero-rated export claim and require full reconstruction of the export or offshore-service evidence. If the substantiation is insufficient, the supply is recharacterised as taxable at 15%, the GST is clawed back, and use-of-money interest runs from the original return date. Civil shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 apply progressively: up to 20% for a significant tax position, 40% for gross carelessness, 100% for an abusive tax position, and 150% for evasion or intentional wrongdoing. Late filing and late payment penalties also accrue in addition to the GST liability. In serious cases involving knowingly false GST returns or deliberately fabricated export documentation, criminal prosecution may result in imprisonment under the Tax Administration Act 1994. The default reassessment period is four years from the end of the taxable period, extended to seven years in cases of fraud or evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) - no separate foreign exchange administration exists; RBNZ is the central bank and prudential regulator under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 1989.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand maintains virtually complete convertibility on both current and capital account. There are no exchange control acts, no restrictions on external balances, no surrender requirements, and no central bank approval required for cross-border capital inflows or outflows. The New Zealand dollar is freely floating and tradeable both onshore and offshore. For a non-resident-owned esports community platform, inbound share capital or shareholder loans may be converted into NZD with any authorized Registered Bank at market rates. Profit remittance and dividend distributions are not blocked by FX legislation, but distributions must satisfy the solvency test under the Companies Act 1993 and must comply with New Zealand non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) rules and any applicable double tax agreement. Payments of royalties, software licensing fees, or tournament services must be priced at arm's length and must comply with thin-capitalization and transfer pricing provisions for the 5820 software publishing activity. Banks will apply enhanced scrutiny to beneficial ownership, source of funds, and the economic purpose of every inbound transfer under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009. There is no practical restriction on holding foreign-currency accounts or invoicing in USD/EUR, but annual financial statements and IRD returns must evidence all FX gains and losses.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender requirement applies in New Zealand. There is no mandatory timeline for conversion and no percentage of foreign currency receipts that must be converted into NZD. Exporters and service providers may retain 100% of export proceeds in any currency and in any account, subject only to normal commercial arrangements with their bank and to reporting of taxable income in NZD in accordance with New Zealand IFRS and IRD requirements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (NZD) / Multi-Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account (NZD)
Corporate Current Account (NZD/USD) for FX and SWIFT clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Fintech EMI viability is Conditional / Medium. New Zealand does not grant full banking licenses to offshore digital EMIs. Platforms such as Wise, Airwallex, and Stripe Treasury may onboard a New Zealand limited company as a customer for payment initiation, conversion, or merchant settlement, but they are not Registered Banks under the Banking (Prudential Supervision) Act 1989 and cannot provide the same NZD clearing assurance, RBNZ settlement, or deposit-taking status. For this esports platform, Stripe and PayPal are acceptable only as merchant acquiring rails for tournament tickets, membership, and digital goods; all substantive corporate treasury, capital injections, prize pool disbursements, and FX transactions must be settled through a Tier 1 New Zealand bank. An offshore EMI holding funds for a New Zealand entity must either be locally licensed as a financial service provider or use a New Zealand bank as settlement partner; otherwise the concentration risk, safeguarding risk, and audit complexity make it unsuitable as the primary treasury vehicle.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Under the AML/CFT Act 2009, a Tier 1 New Zealand bank must identify the company and its beneficial owners, but a physical in-branch appearance by every director is not a blanket statutory mandate for a low-risk company. Most major New Zealand banks accept remote digital identity verification using live video, certified electronic identification, and high-resolution certified copies of passports, the Companies Office extract, certificate of incorporation, and any trust deed. However, New Zealand company law requires at least one director to be resident in New Zealand or Australia, and that director will normally be the primary relationship contact or mandated co-signatory. A consular proxy opening is not a recognized New Zealand banking procedure; if the sole overseas director cannot attend in person, the bank may require a New Zealand-resident director, a local attorney acting under a notarized power of attorney, or an enhanced interview at a recognized overseas branch of the same banking group.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholders and offshore trust ownership structure obscures the natural-person controller and source of wealth.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a Companies Office full extract, certificate of incorporation, shareholders register, directors register, complete group ownership chart, beneficial-ownership declaration for every 25% or greater interest, any relevant trust deed, audited or accountant-certified source-of-wealth statement, and bank reference letters from existing financial institutions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection structured as intercompany loan or third-party funding without clear economic substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarized share subscription or intercompany loan agreement, source bank statements covering at least 12 months, certified board resolution approving the injection, projected income statement and esports tournament business plan, IRD registration confirmation, and a tax accountant memorandum on debt versus equity characterization.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Esports platform perceived as connected to gambling, crypto-assets, or unlicensed prize-pool gaming despite the stated low-risk standard.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a legal opinion confirming that no Class 4 gambling license is required under the Gambling Act 2003 and that tournament prize pools are not gambling proceeds, the published anti-cheating and AML policy, player wallet operational controls, segregation of sponsor funds from prize liabilities, current Stripe and PayPal merchant agreements, and historical payout processing records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the digital front-end community platform and actual outbound cash flows to overseas players and tournament winners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a batch payout register, player KYC and identity verification records, tax withholding certificates or treaty position statements, tournament terms and conditions, reconciliation of the platform ledger to bank statements, and a documented policy that beneficiaries in higher-risk jurisdictions require enhanced due diligence before any payout.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound shareholder capital or shareholder loan proceeds must be routed through a Tier 1 New Zealand bank account using SWIFT MT103 with an unambiguous payment detail block such as 'Share Capital Subscription / Shareholder Loan Agreement dated [date] / Non-resident direct investment - NZ Limited'. The bank will record the required Balance of Payments investment purpose code, typically a foreign direct investment code, for RBNZ statistical reporting. New Zealand has no capital verification certificate regime; instead, the company must execute a share allotment resolution, make the corresponding share register entry under section 89 of the Companies Act 1993, notify the IRD of the shareholder details, and have the external accountant issue a capital verification letter confirming that the funds were received and properly classified. All inbound amounts must be fully explained with source-of-funds evidence before conversion into NZD, and any third-party remitter must provide an authorization letter if the remitter is not the beneficial owner.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Tournament prize payouts, platform sponsorship settlements, and trade disbursements should be executed through the primary Tier 1 New Zealand bank using SWIFT MT103 direct wires for standard Forex and operational payments, with clear payment codes for services, licensing, or prize pools as required by the receiving jurisdiction. For larger trade-related disbursements, an irrevocable commercial letter of credit, typically payable at sight, should be used to secure the payment obligation for imported technology, hardware, or event services; documentary collections under D/P or D/A terms are permissible only where counterparty credit risk has been formally accepted by management. All foreign-currency disbursements should be covered by a prior bank FX quote to fix the NZD cost, and the platform should keep is a complete beneficiary audit trail for every outbound payment to demonstrate compliance with New Zealand AML/CFT obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts (NZD/USD, NZD/EUR, NZD/CNY, etc.) with an authorized New Zealand Registered Bank, typically up to 12 months and documented under an ISDA Master Agreement or bank FX master agreement.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible in New Zealand but are not necessary for NZD because the currency is fully deliverable; if an offshore NDF counterparty is used, the transaction must be supported by underlying commercial exposure and documented locally for derivative disclosure purposes.

Cross-currency swaps between NZD and USD or EUR are permissible for term-matching debt or shareholder loan exposures, subject to bank credit approval, ISDA documentation, and compliance with the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; hedging must be limited to genuinely forecast tournament, licensing, and prize-pool exposures and must not create speculative leverage.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Companies Office Annual Return filed under the Companies Act 1993 (section 208)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Registrar of Companies, Companies Office, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the company's annual return date, which is the anniversary of incorporation unless the Registrar has approved a different return date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fee of NZD 60.00 prescribed under the Companies (Fees) Regulations; the company is placed in default; continued non-filing for two consecutive annual return cycles triggers a formal removal warning and administrative strike-off from the New Zealand Companies Register under Part 17 of the Companies Act 1993.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements and auditor's report (conditional on the company becoming 'large' or qualifying as an FMC reporting entity)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, New Zealand Companies Office, with the audit report issued by a licensed auditor under the Auditor Regulation Act 2011
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 20 working days after the date the financial statements are signed, and in any event no later than 6 months after the company's balance date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is an offence under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; a company may be fined up to NZD 10,000 and each director up to NZD 5,000; continued default may also contribute to removal from the Companies Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Inland Revenue), New Zealand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 7 July following the income year; for a non-standard balance date, the return is due by the 7th day of the second month after the balance date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties apply under the Tax Administration Act 1994: NZD 250 for the first month and NZD 50 per month thereafter up to NZD 500; late payment penalties and use-of-money interest are also assessed on unpaid tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is mandatory in New Zealand if the company is not an exempt company. The company is not exempt if it is an FMC reporting entity under the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013; or it is a 'large company' under section 45 of the Financial Reporting Act 2013; or any shareholder or group of shareholders holding at least 5% of the voting shares validly requests an audit. A company is generally 'large' when it breaches the small-company thresholds: total assets at balance date exceeding NZD 33 million, or total annual revenue exceeding NZD 10 million, or 50 or more full-time equivalent employees, assessed on a consecutive-period basis. A small company below those thresholds may waive the audit only by unanimous shareholder agreement while it remains small. The audit must be carried out by a licensed auditor recognised under the Auditor Regulation Act 2011.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand equivalents to International Financial Reporting Standards (NZ IFRS) apply to Tier 1 reporting entities; Tier 2 entities apply NZ IFRS with the Reduced Disclosure Regime (NZ IFRS RDR). Small non-publicly-accountable companies may prepare financial statements under the simplified reporting framework accepted by the External Reporting Board (XRB) where no statutory audit is triggered; if a large or FMC reporting entity, financial statements must comply with general purpose accounting standards under the Financial Reporting Act 2013.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand does not currently impose a standalone annual ultimate beneficial owner confirmation filing on ordinary private companies. The company must maintain an accurate share register and update that register for every transfer and allotment; all share allotments must be notified to the Registrar within 20 working days, and director changes must be notified within 20 working days. There is no 30-day share-transfer filing to the Companies Office; transfers take effect when recorded in the Register of Members, and the next annual return confirms the resulting shareholder base. Where the esports platform becomes an AML/CFT reporting entity, it must maintain customer due diligence and beneficial-ownership identification records in accordance with the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of shareholder and board meetings
Records of registered office and address for service

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 - USD 30,000 per annum for a small-to-mid-size non-listed New Zealand company, depending on complexity, NZ IFRS requirements, and transaction volumes

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: New Zealand offers a refundable R&D tax credit of 15% of eligible R&D expenditure, with a cash-out option for loss-making companies in limited circumstances. There is no patent box, no special economic zone income tax holiday, and no preferential free-zone regime. The imputation credit system avoids double taxation at shareholder level. Preparatory or transitional costs may be deductible where directly related to assessable income, but no statutory tax holiday applies.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (subject to at least 49% shareholder continuity at all times; if a greater than 49% discontinuity occurs, the loss offset is available only if the company also satisfies the business continuity test)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: IR4 (Company Income Tax Return) filed electronically via Inland Revenue's myIR portal or IRD-approved e-filing software; non-resident companies subject to New Zealand income tax on New Zealand-source income may be required to file the same form through a New Zealand agent or the non-resident company's New Zealand representative.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; provisional tax is payable in three instalments during the year for companies on a standard 31 March balance date.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a standard 31 March balance date, the IR4 must be filed by 7 July immediately following the balance date. A tax agent may obtain an extension of time to file, normally shifting the filing deadline to 31 March of the following year. Provisional tax instalments are due on 28 August, 15 January and 7 May (for standard balance-date companies using the uplift method). Terminal tax is due on 7 July for a standard 31 March company unless a valid extension applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total income before deductions (gross income). This includes worldwide business income for a New Zealand tax-resident company.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: As the entity is a New Zealand-incorporated Ltd, it is a New Zealand tax resident and must declare all global revenue. Include all tournament platform fees, membership subscriptions, in-app purchases, sponsorship revenue, advertising income and any foreign exchange gains. If the taxpayer were a non-resident company, only New Zealand-source income attributable to a New Zealand permanent establishment should be reported. E-sports platform revenue receivable from foreign users for services performed outside New Zealand must be carefully sourced to avoid double taxation and to claim available treaty tie-breaker or PE relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total expenses and deductions incurred in producing assessable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only expenses that are actually incurred and deductible under the Income Tax Act 2007. For New Zealand resident entities, cross-border payments to related non-resident parties (e.g., data centre fees, platform licensing costs, marketing, management and royalties) must satisfy the arm's length standard of s GC 13 and the general anti-avoidance rule in s BG 1. Entertainment expenses are only 50% deductible in New Zealand. Interest deductions on debt used to fund foreign group assets may be limited by the thin capitalisation / interest limitation rules. For non-resident companies, only expenses attributable to the New Zealand PE may be deducted, and head-office allocations must be reimbursed at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net profit or net loss (Box 1 minus Box 2).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm that the net amount is supported by management accounts and reconciles to the Stripe/PayPal transaction reports. If the result is a loss, the loss may be carried forward only if continuity of beneficial ownership of at least 49% is maintained throughout any period between the loss year and the year of offset. Non-resident shareholding changes, transfers between related persons and look-through ownership must be traced for continuity purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Losses carried forward from prior income years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter only losses that satisfy s IA 4 (ownership continuity) and, if applicable, the business continuity test under s IA 5. Non-resident investors should document the entire chain of ownership to prove 49% continuity. Losses cannot be offset against income in a foreign jurisdiction; New Zealand losses are available only against New Zealand assessable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deduction of losses carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure there is no double counting of prior-year loss adjustments. For non-residents, this box should represent only the New Zealand-source taxable income, after applying any specific sourcing provisions and any treaty provisions that allocate profits exclusively to the other state absent a permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax calculated on net taxable income at the company rate (28%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply 28% to Box 5 unless a special rate applies (e.g., a non-resident company not carrying on a business in New Zealand may be subject to different NRWT/schedule tax mechanisms but still files an IR4 if it has a New Zealand taxable presence). Foreign tax credits under the Income Tax Act 2007 and any relevant DTA can be used to relieve double taxation on foreign-source income reported by the New Zealand entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits: provisional tax paid, resident withholding tax (RWT), typical dividends, imputation credits, foreign tax credits, and other credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders are not generally entitled to imputation credits, and no imputation credit should be claimed by a non-resident receiving a dividend. For the New Zealand Ltd entity, if it receives fully imputed dividends from a New Zealand company, imputation credits are allowed. Foreign tax credits must be supported by foreign tax returns and tax residency certificates. Unsupported RWT or imputation credit claims will be disallowed and may attract shortfall penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Residual tax payable or refund due after deducting credits from tax calculated on Box 6.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If residual tax is payable, pay it by the terminal tax date; if refundable, ensure all credits are substantiated. Underpayments attract use of money interest and late payment penalties. A refund claim by a non-resident may require a New Zealand bank account or a valid IRD number and may be delayed until the return is filed and any treaty relief is confirmed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties accrue at NZ$50 per month for each month the IR4 remains outstanding, with maximum late filing penalty exposure of NZ$250. If tax remains unpaid, Inland Revenue imposes an initial late payment penalty of 1% of unpaid tax and a further 1% monthly penalty for continuing non-payment, plus use of money interest at the prescribed rate (currently approximately 8.78% per annum). Civil shortfall penalties under Tax Administration Act 1994, s 141 can reach 150% of the tax shortfall for evasion or a similar offence. Knowingly furnishing a false IR4 is a criminal offence under s 143B of the Tax Administration Act 1994, carrying a fine of up to NZ$150,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% statutory Non-Resident Withholding Tax (NRWT) on dividends paid by a New Zealand company to a non-resident shareholder. DTA-protocol rates commonly reduce the rate for direct dividends to between 0% and 15% depending on the beneficial ownership, holding percentage and treaty partner. Fully imputed dividends do not eliminate NRWT; imputation credits attach for the benefit of New Zealand resident shareholders only.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke reduced NRWT under a Double Tax Agreement, the non-resident beneficial owner must obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by its jurisdiction of residence and provide a completed beneficial ownership declaration to the New Zealand payer before payment. The payer must retain the TRC, the declaration, and a statement that the non-resident is not acting as an agent, nominee or conduit. The reduced rate is applied at source only when the paperwork is held at the time the payment is made; otherwise the full 30% NRWT must be deducted and the non-resident may recover the excess through an annual non-resident tax return or a refund application to Inland Revenue. Inland Revenue may scrutinise the arrangement for sham or treaty shopping, so the recipient must show real business substance, economic ownership and unfettered use of the income.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory NRWT on interest is 15%. If the lender is an unrelated non-resident and the borrower is an approved issuer, a 2% Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) can replace NRWT. On royalties, the statutory NRWT rate is 15%. Under New Zealand's DTAs, interest rates are usually reduced to 10% or 0%, and royalties to 10% or 5%, depending on the treaty and the intellectual property type. Related-party interest and royalty payments remain subject to transfer pricing rules, thin capitalisation limitations and the economic substance requirement; a mere contractual payment without genuine functions, assets or risks in the recipient jurisdiction will be re-characterised.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No statutory Local File or Master File preparation threshold is prescribed in New Zealand domestic law; however, Inland Revenue expects contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation for all material cross-border related-party transactions. Country-by-Country (CbC) reporting is mandatory for multinational groups with consolidated group revenue of EUR 750 million or more (approximately NZD 1.136 billion). Even below that threshold, the e-sports platform must maintain transfer pricing documentation sufficient to demonstrate that intercompany platform licence fees, management fees, server costs, and profit allocations are at arm's length.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: New Zealand does not have a standalone OECD-style Economic Substance Regulation (ESR), but economic substance is embedded in the general anti-avoidance rule (Income Tax Act 2007, s BG 1), the business continuity test for losses, permanent establishment rules, and the arm's length doctrine. The Inland Revenue will disregard artificial or contrived arrangements that lack commercial substance, and will re-allocate profits to the jurisdiction where the core income-generating activities (CIGA) — such as platform development, matchmaking algorithms, tournament management, risk-taking and strategic decision-making — are actually performed. A New Zealand Ltd that is merely a mailbox or booking agent without employees, premises, contracts or operational control over the e-sports platform will fail substance audit and be treated as a sham, exposing directors to personal liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly omitting or misreporting revenue from Stripe and PayPal settlement records for the e-sports tournament platform, creating false invoices, inflating deductions, destroying records, or failing to file the IR4 to conceal New Zealand-source income. This includes directing players' payments to offshore personal accounts and not reporting those amounts in Box 1 of the IR4.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax Administration Act 1994, s 143B (evasion or similar offence): a person committing tax evasion is liable to a fine of up to NZ$150,000 and/or imprisonment for up to 5 years. In addition, s 141 of the Tax Administration Act imposes a civil shortfall penalty equal to 150% of the tax shortfall for evasion or intentional wrongdoing, plus use of money interest and late payment penalties. The Commissioner may also issue a default assessment and offset any credits, and any agent who knowingly assists is separately liable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced where the company is used as a vehicle for tax fraud. Directors can be made personally and jointly liable for unpaid company tax under Tax Administration Act 1994, s 149 in respect of unremitted withholding or deduction obligations. Criminal sanctions under s 143B extend to directors who knowingly sign or cause false returns to be filed. Civil asset restraints and recovery orders may be obtained under the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009, including freezing of personal bank accounts, real property and cryptocurrency wallets. Directors with an active arrest warrant are placed on border alerts, resulting in a travel ban / blacklist preventing departure from New Zealand, and may be disqualified from managing companies under Companies Act 1994, s 382. Imprisonment of up to 5 years may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing outbound dividends, royalties or interest through a zero-tax intermediary company in a treaty jurisdiction that has no real business, no staff, no premises and no independent control over the funds, solely to claim a reduced non-resident withholding tax rate on payments from the New Zealand e-sports platform. The structure is presented as tax-motivated and uses a Tax Residency Certificate from the intermediary jurisdiction while the beneficial owner remains the New Zealand controller or foreign parent without treaty entitlement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The arrangement is void under the general anti-avoidance rule in s BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007 and payments may be re-characterised as taxable profits in New Zealand. Under Tax Administration Act 1994, s 141C (abusive tax position), a shortfall penalty of 100% of the tax shortfall applies, with interest; if fraud is established, the 150% evasion penalty under s 141 and the criminal offence under s 143B apply. The payer is also responsible for unpaid NRWT, and a failure to withhold and remit NRWT triggers recovery from the payer plus a 20% late filing and non-deduction penalty exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who structure or approve the conduit may be personally liable for the unpaid NRWT and penalties under Tax Administration Act 1994, s 149 because the liability arises as a deduction and remittance obligation. Courts may pierce the corporate veil if the conduit is found to be a sham, making directors personally accountable for the diverted funds. Criminal prosecution under s 143B can result in imprisonment; the Criminal Proceeds (Recovery) Act 2009 may be used to seize assets acquired from the scheme, and directors may be added to the border alert / travel ban list, preventing them from leaving New Zealand during investigation or after conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Aggressive Transfer Pricing / Profit Stripping Through Related-Party Payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging inflated management fees, platform royalties, server hosting fees or interest from the New Zealand e-sports entity to an offshore related company, while the New Zealand entity retains no economic substance, employees, assets or decision-making functions. The intercompany charges erode the New Zealand taxable base, and no contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is prepared to prove arm's length conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue may adjust the consideration to an arm's length result under s GC 13 of the Income Tax Act 2007, re-assess the New Zealand company to additional taxable income, and impose a shortfall penalty under Tax Administration Act 1994, s 141B for taking an unacceptable tax position (20% of the shortfall) or, where the arrangement is considered abusive, 100% under s 141C. The anti-avoidance rules in s BG 1 may cancel the pricing structure entirely. Interest limitation rules and non-resident withholding tax on the service/interest payments may also be triggered. Criminal liability under s 143B arises if the documentation is fabricated to conceal the arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Company directors who knowingly implement sham transfer pricing arrangements may have the corporate veil pierced for having used the company for a dishonest purpose, allowing creditors and Inland Revenue to recover unpaid tax from their personal assets. Directors may also be liable for insolvent trading under Companies Act 1994, ss 135 and 136 if the excessive service fees render the company unable to pay its tax debts. Court orders can include asset restitution, prohibition on leaving New Zealand (travel ban), blacklisting from tax compliance and company management, and imprisonment for up to 5 years for criminal tax evasion or fraud.
